answer_key_agreement: My independent covered-options answer matched the keyed letter on 15 of 15 items.
comparability_note: The r3 and r4 reviews were conducted by different fresh reviewers against the same calibrated rubric. Defect counts are the comparable quantity and reviewer variance cannot be excluded; r4 reviewed 15 items against r3's 13.

defect_comparison_with_r3.note: The r4 numeric defect is the propagated McBurney's point unit error, not an arithmetic failure; both stated derived scores recomputed exactly, which is the class the r3 numeric defect belonged to.

rationale_enhancement_opportunities: All four options are age-appropriate wheezing diagnoses; first-episode status, seasonality and symmetric findings are all findings a clinician would document, so no clause reads as written-to-negate.

Parity survives because the set is two monitoring strategies plus two tests rather than three tests against a lone no-test key; the shared-bay detail earns option C a real indication instead of leaving it inert.

Superficial suctioning is a lower-tier intervention than oxygen, but the crusted nares make it a live bedside first move rather than a straw man; repeat settled saturations of 87 and 88 percent are internally consistent with the 90 percent threshold in the key.

defects.detail: Galactocele carries no fever, no erythema and no systemic illness, all three of which the stem supplies, so it is dead on arrival while ductal narrowing and abscess remain genuinely competitive; the option set effectively has two real competitors, not three.

ordered_item_verdicts.failure_reason: Option C galactocele is a non-inflammatory benign mass offered against a stem with 38.4 C fever, tachycardia and spreading erythema, putting it at least two severity tiers below the key.
rationale_enhancement_opportunities: The abscess discriminator (uniformly firm and merging into surrounding tissue, versus a palpable fluid collection in a well-defined area) is the strongest part of the item and could carry a fourth option built on the same spectrum instead of the off-spectrum galactocele.

defects.detail: The lead-in asks which investigation should characterise the residual area; a milk culture answers a microbiological rather than a structural question, and the item's own rebuttal concedes it leaves 'a structural question that a culture cannot answer'.

ordered_item_verdicts.failure_reason: Option B sterile milk culture is discardable from the lead-in alone, because a milk culture cannot characterise a residual breast mass.
rationale_enhancement_opportunities: The smooth, freely mobile skin finding is decisive against the inflammatory-carcinoma competitor and is natural breast-examination documentation, so it does not read as terminal exclusion.
The phlegmon-versus-collection discrimination against needle aspiration is the item's real teaching point and is well stated.

defects.detail: Dangle feeding, pumping the breast empty after every feed and the silicone shield are each named in the stem and each appears as a distractor; a candidate with no content knowledge reaches B by the heuristic that what the patient is already doing is what the question is correcting.

ordered_item_verdicts.failure_reason: The stem enumerates exactly three practices the patient has already adopted, which map one-to-one onto the three distractors, so the key is identifiable as the only option not pre-enacted in the stem.
rationale_enhancement_opportunities: The hyperlactation mechanism against pumping to empty is the strongest discriminator in the set and is correctly tied to the instruction to express only the volume the infant consumes.
The cue would be defused by grounding only one or two of the practices in the stem, or by making the key itself something she is doing incorrectly in degree rather than in kind.

defects.detail: The stem places maximal tenderness 2 cm from the right ASIS and the key decisive point asserts McBurney's point lies 1.5 to 2 cm from the ASIS along the line to the umbilicus; the standard figure is 1.5 to 2 inches, so the stated location is an inch-to-centimetre conversion error that puts the point essentially on the iliac spine.
The anatomical definition of McBurney's point stated in the key rationale and reproduced in the stem's examination finding is incorrect as written.

Options A, B and D are all gynecologic (pelvic inflammatory disease, ovarian torsion, tubo-ovarian abscess) and the key is the only non-gynecologic diagnosis, so the key is the categorical odd one out; combined with a wholly negative bimanual examination the answer is reachable from option-set structure.

ordered_item_verdicts.failure_reason: McBurney's point is misplaced at 2 cm from the ASIS (the accepted description is 1.5 to 2 inches, roughly 4 to 5 cm, or one third of the ASIS-to-umbilicus line), and the key is the lone non-gynecologic option among three gynecologic diagnoses.
rationale_enhancement_opportunities: The bimanual findings themselves are natural documentation for a young woman with right lower quadrant pain and do not by themselves constitute terminal exclusion; the parity problem is the homogeneity of the three distractors, not the presence of the examination.

The stated Alvarado score of 5 recomputes exactly from the stem's own findings: migration 1, anorexia 1, nausea 1, right lower quadrant tenderness 2, no rebound 0, temperature 37.1 C below 37.3 C 0, white cell count 9.6 not above 10 0, neutrophils 64 percent not above 75 percent 0.

Serial observation is the lone non-imaging option, but it is a legitimate diagnostic strategy under a 'next step in diagnosis' lead-in and sits on the same algorithm as the imaging choices, so parity holds.
The closing body mass index and renal function sentence is a genuine modality-selection consideration rather than a clause written to falsify options.

defects.detail: Antibiotics-first is a strategy for uncomplicated appendicitis only; in florid generalised peritonitis with radiographic free perforation no candidate holds it as a live option, so it contributes no discrimination.

ordered_item_verdicts.failure_reason: Option A, intravenous antibiotics alone with planned reassessment, sits two severity tiers below the key in a patient with a rigid abdomen, four-quadrant rebound, temperature 38.7 C, heart rate 118 and free perforation on computed tomography.
rationale_enhancement_opportunities: The computed tomography phrase 'diffuse throughout the peritoneal cavity rather than walled off' does double duty against options B and C; the same information as a radiology-style 'no organised collection' would read less like a written-in negation.
Percutaneous drainage and interval appendectomy are both genuinely competitive and are correctly separated from the key by the contained-versus-free contamination distinction.

The thyroid stimulating hormone result maps one-to-one onto option D, but thyroid stimulating hormone and complete blood count are routine baseline investigations a clinician documents in a depression assessment, so the clause earns its place rather than reading as terminal exclusion.

Option D is the least competitive of the three, since it is settled by a single stated laboratory value rather than by clinical reasoning; a competitor requiring interpretation would raise reasoning demand.
The alcohol and medication line covers substance effects, which the plan listed as an exclusion but which does not appear as an option; this is handled in the stem rather than left unaddressed.

defects.detail: Option B, applying a suicide risk rating scale to set disposition, and option D, starting an antidepressant with review in 48 hours, are not live options for a man who has named a date, holds the means at home and is psychotic; both are severity-mismatched rather than competitive.

Option C is the only inpatient disposition in a set whose other three members are all community-level actions, so the key is the categorical odd one out and is identifiable without weighing the clinical detail.
Every risk feature in the stem points the same way with no counterweight, so the item tests recognition of an extreme presentation rather than a discrimination at the level the plan describes.

ordered_item_verdicts.failure_reason: Against a stem with dated intent, an in-home shotgun and nihilistic delusions, the three distractors are all outpatient actions two or more severity tiers below the key, and the key is the lone disposition option in the set.
rationale_enhancement_opportunities: The sister's four-hour distance and same-night departure is a legitimate supervision fact rather than a negating clause, and it is the most useful discriminator in the item.

A version pitting immediate admission against a same-day psychiatric assessment with continuous observation, or against certification under mental health legislation, would restore both parity and granularity.

defects.detail: The option C rebuttal states that supervised exercise is 'first-line monotherapy for mild depression and a second-line adjunctive treatment at moderate severity'; CANMAT positions exercise as first-line monotherapy for mild to moderate major depressive disorder and second-line adjunctive for moderate to severe illness, so the stated band is narrowed and the discriminator does not hold as written.

ordered_item_verdicts.failure_reason: The discriminator offered against supervised exercise misstates its recommended severity band, since current Canadian guidance recommends exercise as first-line monotherapy for mild to moderate major depressive disorder, not for mild depression alone.
rationale_enhancement_opportunities: The key survives the correction, because explicit patient preference for medication plus a six-month psychotherapy wait settles the choice, but the exercise option should be excluded on preference and severity of functional impairment rather than on a misquoted severity band.
The access and preference details are decisive rather than exclusionary, and they mirror the guideline's own stated basis for choosing between modalities.
Three separate stem clauses (preference, waiting list, shift work) all push toward the same answer, which makes the item somewhat over-determined.

The internal numbers are coherent: equal cancer-specific mortality per 1000 person-years and an identical median age at death of 71 years alongside a 1.7-year gap in survival measured from diagnosis is precisely the lead-time signature.

Three stem facts (comparable baseline health, equal number of cancers diagnosed, similar grade and growth-rate distribution) each negate one distractor, which is close to a checklist; each is nonetheless standard reporting for a randomised screening trial and is needed to leave a single defensible answer, so terminal exclusion is not triggered.

defects.detail: The key is the sole option that presents both a benefit and a harm figure, and the only one that is not an appended persuasive sentence; option structure alone identifies it under a lead-in that asks which revision best protects autonomy.

Adding a medical officer of health endorsement and announcing that a reminder will follow are transparently uptake levers rather than autonomy protections, so both are eliminated by reading the lead-in without engaging the scenario numbers.

ordered_item_verdicts.failure_reason: Options A, C and D are all uptake-promoting additions while the key is the only revision that supplies decision-relevant information, so the key is the categorical odd one out and the distractors are discardable straight off the autonomy lead-in.
rationale_enhancement_opportunities: The scenario numbers are internally coherent: a 30 percent relative reduction is compatible with roughly 4 avoided deaths per 1000 over 10 years at a plausible baseline risk, and 100 needless recalls per 1000 is the harm side the letter omits.

Option D is the only genuinely competitive distractor, because a raw count of cancers found is a real figure that fails only for lack of a denominator; three variations on that theme would make a much harder item.

The capacity figures are internally consistent: 3000 expected positives against 900 confirmatory procedures a year and 200 expected treatment candidates against 120 treatment slots, with an existing 14-week wait.

The rebuttal of the staged-rollout option ('a smaller district still feeds the same queue') is the weakest discriminator in the set, since a pilot sized to 900 procedures would in fact fit the pathway; the durable objection is that the treatment service is under-resourced in aggregate and the 14-week wait is untouched, and stating that would close the option more cleanly.

recurring_systemic_failure_modes: Lone-key option category: in three items (SURG-I01, PSY-I02, PHELO-I02) the three distractors form a homogeneous class (gynecologic diagnoses, community-level actions, uptake-promoting letter edits) and the key is the only member of a different class, making it reachable from option structure alone.

Severity-tier mismatch in one distractor per item: a benign non-inflammatory mass against febrile mastitis, antibiotics alone against generalised peritonitis, and a risk rating scale or 48-hour antidepressant review against an armed dated suicide plan; each set therefore carries only two genuine competitors.

Distractors negated by a single stem line rather than by clinical reasoning, so they add no discrimination even where they are not formally weak (thyroid stimulating hormone against the hypothyroid option, absence of improvement against the milk culture).
Stem-enacted distractors: OBGYN-I03 names all three wrong practices in the stem and leaves the key as the only option the patient is not already doing, an eliminable-by-pattern cue.

Precision failure on a borrowed anatomical figure: McBurney's point stated at 1.5 to 2 cm rather than 1.5 to 2 inches, carried from the source claim into the stem's examination finding, indicating derived figures are not being sanity-checked against the anatomy or units they describe.
Guideline severity bands narrowed when writing distractor rebuttals (exercise as first-line monotherapy), so the discriminator asserts more than the source supports even though the key is unaffected.
retest_assessment: MIXED: the answer key held on 15 of 15 and pediatrics passed cleanly, but 8 items failed on option-set construction rather than on clinical content, with three lone-key category failures, five severity-mismatched or lead-in-discardable distractors, and one propagated unit error, indicating that stem and key quality are ahead of distractor and option-set discipline.
verification_method: Fresh reviewer given only assembled stems, lead-ins, options, keys and rationales, plus the planned item form, learner decision and intended key for fidelity judgements, with no access to the construction record, the seed pack or the evidence packet. Each item was solved with the options covered before any judgement, and every stated derived value was recomputed from the stem's own findings.
